action_sequence_structure: labels 0-23 = banked L1->L2 prefix from results/arc_loop_solve_r11l.json; labels 24-81 = this session's L3 solve (13 clicks place the f-piece on its template, 45 clicks route the e-piece's four handles through the west channel and east corridor to overlap its template)
novel_mechanics_found: L3 mechanics fully reverse-engineered: (1) BLACK diamond = currently-SELECTED handle (the mysterious color-0 handle was just leftover selection from L2, not a locked handle). (2) Handle moves are radius-limited teleports: click destination must be within EUCLIDEAN distance 8 of the handle center ((8,0) ok, (7,4)=8.06 rejected) and on open background; wall ('a'-colored) destinations and destinations whose 13-cell diamond footprint clips walls/template-dots are silently rejected (click still consumed). Hops OVER walls are allowed - only the destination matters. (3) The piece teleports to floor(mean(handle centers)) after each handle move; if that position overlaps wall terrain the game is an instant GAME_OVER (discovered the hard way). (4) col-0 black stripe = 64-click per-level budget; hits 0 -> GAME_OVER. (5) GameAction.RESET mid-level OR after GAME_OVER restarts the current level fresh (64 budget, pieces reset, levels_completed preserved) - GAME_OVER is fully recoverable. env.reset() after GAME_OVER does NOT work (broken state); use RESET or rebuild the env. (6) Placements within Chebyshev 2 of ANOTHER handle (including the other piece's handles) are rejected; Chebyshev 3 is accepted. (7) WIN condition is template OVERLAP, not exact centering - the e-piece locked as soon as its footprint touched the template dots (piece center (49,55) vs template center (53,55)). Template dots turn BLACK when their piece is correctly placed. (8) Wires (color-1 lines linking handles to their piece) occupy cells and block handle placement; they redraw as handles/pieces move, so a blocked cell often clears after moving something else.
narrative: Resolved the 24-label verified prefix, entered L3: two pieces (e,f) each needing to reach a dotted template; f-piece has 2 handles, e-piece has 4 (piece position = floor of the handle-center average). The e-template sits bottom-right but the only piece-safe corridor from the e-piece's start crosses a narrow west channel (piece column must be <=19-22 for rows 24-29), forcing ~330 total handle-sum-displacement - close to the 64-click level budget. Final run: RESET, replayed an optimized f-placement (13 clicks), drove the e-piece with a simulated-and-validated 4-handle choreography plus beam-searched endgame, and won with 5 clicks to spare when the piece touched its template (overlap suffices). Self-ran the offline reproduction gate: 82-label sequence reproduces level 3 from a fresh reset (reached_level=3, reproduced=True). L4 recon shows a large difficulty jump: THREE pieces with 2-3 colors each, six handles, and multiple color-matched multi-part templates - left for a future session (insufficient env-step budget to solve AND gate today).
gotchas: Handle move rejected silently (click consumed) if: dest Euclidean distance > 8, dest on wall, dest diamond footprint clips wall/template dots, or dest within Chebyshev 2 of another handle (any piece's).
Piece position recomputes to floor(mean(handles)) after EVERY handle move - if that overlaps wall terrain it is INSTANT GAME_OVER, so plan the piece's trajectory, not just the handles'.
col-0 stripe = 64-click level budget, decrements ~1 per click (selects, rejected clicks and no-op ACTION1-5 all count); 0 = GAME_OVER.

GameAction.RESET restarts the current level cleanly (fresh 64 budget, pieces reset, levels kept) both mid-level and after GAME_OVER - the safe recovery path. env.reset() after GAME_OVER leaves a broken state; rebuild the env instead.
Win = template OVERLAP (any touch), not exact center; template dots turn black on lock. Avoid dragging a piece across the WRONG piece's template en route (untested but plausibly fatal).
The black diamond is the selection highlight, not a special handle.
Wire (color-1) pixels block handle destinations; they redraw when things move - reorder moves to clear them, and re-check dest cell color==5 immediately before every click.
The e-piece west-channel crossing (piece cols<=19-22, rows 24-29) is the only route between the top region and the bottom - budget the sum-work for the col detour (~330 L1 total).

arc_solver_kit.reproduce()-style replays must contain ONLY actually-executed env.step labels - a manually-stepped RESET that skips the logging wrapper corrupts the extracted sequence (cost one failed gate replay).
